topics.name: Riemann hypothesis
aliases: Lean verification of the Riemann Hypothesis
topics.summary: On November 20, Levent Alpöge released a proof of the Riemann hypothesis as a 17-million-line Lean library, made working with Claude, and the Lean and Mathlib communities certified it as correct the next day.
topics.why_now: Two attempts landed the same day: Alpöge's machine-checked proof, and a 940-page human-written manuscript by Alessandro Masullo aimed at the generalized hypothesis, which readers have since found gaps in. The Hacker News thread on Masullo's announcement drew 2,447 points.

topics.name: full moon beaver moon
topics.summary: The Beaver Moon is the traditional name for November's full moon. In 2026 it reached peak fullness at 14:53 UTC on November 24 and counts as a supermoon.
topics.why_now: The full moon peaked today, November 24, and Space.com describes it as a supermoon.

editorial.brief: Two stories crossed feeds today. Grand Theft Auto VI turned up on Wikipedia, YouTube and Google Trends at once, and the final Avengers: Doomsday trailer drew 55,201,638 YouTube views ahead of its December 18 release. Miss Universe 2026 topped Wikipedia with 394,056 reads, and the rest of the internet sat down for Thanksgiving pie.
editorial.cover_sub: Miss Universe 2026 drew 394,056 Wikipedia reads, half again as many as Ramayana: Part 1 in second place, on a day when every other feed was busy with trailers, pies and Jensen Huang.
editorial.wiki_deck: The pageant led Wikipedia by 1.5 times over its nearest rival. No other feed in the snapshot mentioned it, so why people were reading remains their own business.
editorial.letter_headline: A pageant, a trailer and the pies
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News is anxious about a 1Password security incident and an essay that opens with Holy shit. Lemmy cares about workers' rights and talking AI dolls, Bluesky about Joe Rogan and pie, Mastodon about family and space junk.
editorial.foreign_deck: The wires had Asian stocks falling on an AI wobble and the UN chief urging AI safety talks. Brazil searched reality-show polls, and Japan searched Jensen Huang and Kioxia dividends.
editorial.markets_deck: Jensen Huang draws $6M: one market on a new NVIDIA CEO and one on a fourth affair, both priced at 100 percent. The rest is a Yokohama bout, a Fed bet and Counter-Strike.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 peaked at 1,207,614 players, Dota 2 edged PUBG by 3,436, and something called ROB RUN reached 414,459. On Twitch, TheBurntPeanut held 50,463 viewers, more than xQc and StRoGo combined.
editorial.yt_headline: A music video outranks the Avengers
editorial.yt_note: Jamie Miller's Babydoll leads the trending list on 540,129 views, and the Avengers: Doomsday final trailer sits behind it with 55,201,638. Trending, evidently, is not a head count.
editorial.closing_note: By tomorrow's edition the pies will be eaten and the bathroom scales put right. Miss Universe 2026 will have lost its readers to something else, the trailer will have a bigger number, and the Jensen Huang markets will have fresh odds. The space junk, as Donald Kessler warned in 1978, stays where it is.
wiki_paras: Miss Universe 2026 was the most-read article on Wikipedia, with 394,056 views. Ramayana: Part 1 followed at 268,083, then Ezra Frech at 260,732 and the 35th season of Dancing with the Stars at 205,438. The lead works out at 1.5 times the runner-up, which is comfortable but not crushing.

What drove the reading is not in the data. The pageant appears on no other feed: not Google Trends, not YouTube, not a single social timeline. Its audience arrived, read and left no trace anywhere else in the snapshot. Whatever the crowd wanted to know, it looked it up quietly and told nobody.

The rest of the top five says more about the day than the leader does. Of the five, only Grand Theft Auto VI, fifth with 151,092 views, also showed up on YouTube and in Google Trends. The pageant won the page. The game, spread across three feeds, had the wider day.
letter_paras: Today's snapshot was scattered rather than loud, and no single story owned it. Grand Theft Auto VI and Avengers: Doomsday each crossed feeds, the trailer pulling 55,201,638 views, while Hacker News fixed on a 1Password security incident at 1,314 points. Prediction markets and Japanese search both circled Jensen Huang. It was also Thanksgiving, and two social feeds had already noticed.

The small print repaid a closer look. A GGUF build of Inkling-2-Mini from unsloth logged 2,445,633 Hugging Face downloads, roughly 25 times the original's 96,527. A YouTube playlist promised the best Christmas music of 2027 with five weeks of 2026 still to run. USGS counted 25 quakes above M2.5, the largest an M5.3 off Hengchun, Taiwan. Lemmy gave 599 votes to a German oven.

A same-hour reading matters because the internet keeps no minutes. By tomorrow the trailer will carry a larger number, the Polymarket odds will have moved, and today's pie joke will be gone from every timeline. Taking the snapshot at the same moment each day turns that steady forgetting into a record someone can actually compare against.
